source: I ought not to trust Ophelia. She might be in my uncle's pocket after all. Or far worse.
I'll avenge you, Father. I swear it. Propriety will be restored to this castle.
He really is gone.
Of course I know him, but of what might I be afraid?
Ophelia told me you believed he was dangerous. That he might have some mission here in Elsinore.
What cause would I have to believe that? If anything, he was a great help to me.
Then Ophelia was wrong.
I ought not to trust her. She might be in my uncle's pocket after all. Or far worse.
I believe you, my son.
Father, are you afraid? Are you suffering at all?
No. I don't want to know. I can't. Goodbye, Father. I'll keep my promise. I swear.
My son, listen carefully to me.
I was wrong.
Claudius is not our enemy. A more insidious foe awaits.
I misspoke in accusing my brother of my death. He was driven by something far more peculiar. Quince is such a peculiar man.
He is not human, Hamlet. He is a demon of some twisted persuasion. Or a god. I do not know which.
The Playmaster? Father, are you certain?
How can someone inhuman look so normal?
I do not know. But I do know that I have seen many strange things in this life of mine.
You know I am dead, my son, and yet here I stand before you.
The power we discuss is something greater than the bounds of this world, greater than anything we know.
His can even transcend death. It caused me years of anguish and grief. I was trapped in Elsinore, unable to live or die, in some hellish version of this world where time repeated itself.
And now Ophelia is trapped, too.
Earlier, Ophelia told me that he conspired to kill you, Father. Is it true?
In a manner of speaking. Quince is the one who kept me in that shadowy version of Elsinore. I knew Claudius was trying to murder me from the start. But...
Whenever I stopped him, things only became worse. In one world, your mother drowned herself and took you with her.
In another, Claudius created a conspiracy, then convinced my own men to turn against me and have me imprisoned indefinitely.
Every world was more vile than the world where I did nothing at all.
And so, eventually, I gave up. I lay in that garden for years, broken into three-day spans of time.
Eventually, I did not return to life. And yet my spirit still lingers.
It is Peter Quince's power that keeps me here. Ophelia has helped me realize this. We were merely the puppets to his infinite jest.
Please, my son. Save me. Save my soul. Kill him. It's the only choice I have left.
Merely destroying your uncle will not free me, or Ophelia.
I don't know how to feel about all this.
If what you say is true, then we've got to turn the tables on Quince somehow.
We need to destroy him. For your sake and for Ophelia's.
But what will happen when he's dead? Will you disappear, Father?
I do not know.
My form is feeble. I feel my flesh disintegrating. I must go.
Be careful, my son. Think long upon your plans. I don't wish to cause you any more suffering than I've already brought you.
Father, I'm going to destroy him.
I'm going to free you. I promise.
No matter what might happen afterward.
I believe you now. And my father. I don't understand fully, but I want to.
I wish I had known earlier. Claudius no longer trusts me. The castle watches me like a hungry wolf, waiting for a moment of weakness.
Ophelia, is it true you've seen this all before?
What happens now? What will become of me?
Fortinbras will march on us all. You may survive to see that. You may not.
You sound so strange. It's like all the warmth has gone out of you.
How... many... times have you seen me die?
I don't keep count of deaths any more.
Listen. If this world is truly nothing but a fragment, then begin anew. Start over. Come back.
And when you find me and persuade me again, I'm certain I'll think of the same plan: to turn the play upon the Playmaster.
We'll use his own production to expose him in public, and then I'll take him down.
I'll find you again, Hamlet. I'm sorry.
Go. Do it now. Don't waste another minute in this hell.
I feel hopeful.

source: I've thought of a plan.
We'll turn the play upon the Playmaster. I've been working with him to concoct a performance to shame my uncle in public.
But if we surprise him, and turn the tables on him instead...
Then we can catch him where he can't hide, and kill him before an audience.
And what then? The others will believe we've murdered a man in cold blood.
Come what may. We'll figure it out together.
As long as the two of us are alive, I know we can manage.
Quince is highly intelligent. If we use a performance to trap him, we'll need to surprise him somehow.
If we can get your father's spirit to appear, that may sufficiently frighten him.
He and I can keep Quince distracted while you plunge a blade into his heart.
My thoughts precisely.
It's a shame we aren't in the business of killing. We'd be quite good at it, I think.
You have no idea.
Let's prepare. You speak to your father and tell him of our plan. I'll ready myself when the time comes.
Ophelia, it's time. Are you ready?
I don't know that we can be ready for something quite like this. But I'm going to try.
If something terrible happens to me, you can always try once more, can't you?
I don't know. I think so.
My good playmaster, I've prepared some material of my own.
Oh? Brilliant!
How keen of you, my prince. I don't often relinquish the stage. But you have such charisma when you're in the mood for it.
Come on up, then!
My thanks.
No script! Are you improvising today, my lord?
I certainly am.
Everyone, I have something to tell you. Please, listen carefully.
I know the cloud of death already hangs over Elsinore. Far be it from me to bring more dismal news.
But, nevertheless--
We are all in grave danger. This man, Peter Quince, wishes to cause us great suffering.
In fact, he has. In past worlds—in other versions of the world we live in now.
Er, other worlds?
He's finally broken.
He's telling the truth.
Quince is a murderer. He's orchestrated all of your deaths. The when—the why—is not important.
But if you don't listen to us, you'll all be dead within two days' time.
Ophelia! Get down from there!
What on earth are you doing?
I wouldn't have learned about Quince's plans if it weren't for Ophelia's help. We owe her our lives.
Everything calamitous that's happened as of late—it all has been Peter Quince's doing, his wishes, to see us suffer.
He is treasonous. Indirectly, he organized my father's murder at Claudius's hands.
What is happening?
H-How is such a thing possible?
Stop this at once. I am no murderer, and I don't know what you're talking about!
Clear the stage. This performance is over.
Hamlet. Don't you think this 'play' has gone far enough?
Everyone's looking at you as though-- as if-- this is some bizarre game.
Please. Stop this.
On the contrary, this performance has just begun.
A-a-- a ghost!
Is that...?
King Hamlet's spirit.
No. It can't be. You're dead. I put you into your grave myself!
You again? Haven't you got an empty wall to haunt?
Brother, Gerta, be not afraid.
Hamlet, is that really you?
Gerta, be not afraid.
Everyone, be not afraid.
I come not to destroy, but to rebuild.
It cannot be!
Hamlet? Is that really you?
Are you truly here? Or is this some spirit sent from Hell to claim me at last?
I am a spirit, but not here to claim you, Gerta.
Don't weep, my love. I have heard your prayers and whispers. I was with you in your loneliest moments.
You were never alone. Not for a minute. And now I wish you only happiness.
Oh, Hamlet... i-is... is it true you were murdered?
Yes. It is true.
Look upon your husband's face. You have only to look to see the truth.
Do not hate him, my love. His hand was forced by the plodding pace of fate.
My King, is that really you?
Are you truly here? Or is this some spirit sent from Hell?
I am a spirit, but not here to claim you, Bernardo.
Your Highness, I tried to meet your spirit after... after the first time Hamlet spoke to you.
I am sorry. I am sorry I could not save your life. I know now that Claudius betrayed you.
I swore to serve you faithfully, and when it came to keep you alive, I failed.
You, who were like a father to me.
Don't weep. I have heard your prayers, Bernardo.
You were the most stalwart man any King could hope for. I wish you only happiness.
And do not hate Claudius, my good man. My brother's hand was forced by the plodding pace of fate.
And the one cranking that wheel was Peter Quince.
Peter Quince? This little countryside playmaster? But I don't understand!
He's just a visitor. What reason could he have to desire your death?
Peter Quince? This little countryside playmaster? But I don't understand.
He's just a visitor. How could he possibly have caused your death?
Yes, do explain yourself. I'm merely a humble traveling thespian!
If ever you trusted me, then know also that this man is a danger to you, innocent though he seem.
It is because of him that I linger here in this world, unable to pass on.
It's true, my lords, my ladies. We have to act against him.
Claudius, if you wish to save what remains of your kingdom and its future, help us end this man's life.
Help us, and redeem yourself.
Do not leave me in this state any longer, brother. Let me pass on. Kill this man.
Seize him.
Bernardo, if ever you considered me a friend, or my father a father of your own, help us end this man's life.
Do not leave me in this state any longer, Bernardo. Let me pass on. Kill this man.
Hamlet. Seize the playmaster.
Oh, come now, Claudius. You don't actually want to kill me. All this exhausting, confusing drivel. What does it mean to you?
What difference does it make if you killed your brother? Look at all you gained! Look at the richness of your reward! Doesn't that make it God's own will?
All this is just a misunderstanding. The insane delusions of your insane nephew, who hijacked a community event to make his final stand.
Can't we have him off to an asylum and be done with it?
